headline: Anadarko sale funds debt paydown as oil prices lift profit
summary_short: Ovintiv's Q2 2026 revenue rose 30.0% y/y to $3.01B on higher realized oil prices and NuVista-driven volumes, with net income up 48.5% to $456M; proceeds from the $2.8B Anadarko-asset sale cut long-term debt to $3.70B from $5.33B a year ago.
summary_long: Revenue rose 30% y/y to $3.01B on a 56% jump in realized oil prices (to $100.69/bbl) and higher NuVista-driven volumes, partly offset by lower oil output after the Q2 sale of the Anadarko assets. Operating income rose 94% y/y to $994M and net income rose 48.5% to $456M, absorbing a $337M loss on the Anadarko divestiture booked in other expenses. Sale proceeds ($2.8B, closed April 9) funded repayment of the $1.2B Term Credit Agreement and redemption of $700M senior notes, cutting long-term debt to $3.70B from $5.33B a year ago; Ovintiv also repurchased $345M of stock and paid $0.30/share dividends. In July the company raised 2026 production guidance to 630-645 MBOE/d; capex guidance stands at $2.25-2.35B.

drivers.explanation: Higher realized oil and NGL prices plus a full quarter of NuVista-acquired Montney volumes drove double-digit revenue and earnings growth; Anadarko-sale proceeds funded debt repayment and buybacks even after absorbing a $337M loss on that same divestiture.
Revenue rose on a 56% jump in realized oil prices and higher NGL/gas volumes from the NuVista acquisition, partly offset by lower oil volumes following the Q2 sale of the Anadarko assets.
Gross profit growth is explained by revenue (+30% y/y) rising faster than cost of revenue over the same period.
Margin expansion reflects revenue growth outpacing cost-of-revenue growth over the same period.

Operating income more than doubled y/y on higher realized prices and NuVista volumes; neither Q2 2026 nor Q2 2025 carried a ceiling-test impairment (the $1,485M H1 2026 impairment was booked entirely in Q1).
EBITDA rose with operating income on higher realized prices and added NuVista production, partly offset by higher transportation and processing costs tied to increased volumes.
Net income rose 48.5% despite absorbing a $337M loss on the Anadarko divestiture booked in other expenses, as operating income growth from higher prices and volumes more than offset it.
EPS rose with net income, though per-share gains were partly diluted by a higher weighted-average share count following the NuVista stock-and-cash acquisition.
Cash from operations rose with higher realized prices and NuVista-added volumes, consistent with the reported Non-GAAP Cash Flow increase to $1,256M for the quarter.
Long-term debt fell as the company redeemed $700M of senior notes and repaid its $1.2B Term Credit Agreement using proceeds from the $2.8B Anadarko-asset sale.
